what_MonetaConfig_ephemeral_guarantees.guarantee_verbatim_from_vendor: If 'storage_uri' not in overrides, it is set to f"moneta-ephemeral://{uuid.uuid4().hex}" (api.py:154-157). Docstring: 'Each call returns a config whose URI does not collide with any prior or concurrent ephemeral() call in the same process.' storage_uri MAY be overridden by the caller, in which case the auto-generated URI is replaced.
what_MonetaConfig_ephemeral_guarantees.the_lock_it_pairs_with: moneta/api.py:169 `_ACTIVE_URIS: set[str]` — a process-level registry, NOT a scalar. Moneta.__init__ acquires a process-level lock ON config.storage_uri; close()/context-exit releases it. Two live handles on the SAME storage_uri raise MonetaResourceLockedError (api.py:180-183).
what_MonetaConfig_ephemeral_guarantees.the_load_bearing_consequence: The substrate's own contract is URI-KEYED EXCLUSION, not global exclusion. N live handles are legal iff their N URIs are distinct. A process-global SCALAR singleton in SYNAPSE would be STRICTLY STRONGER than the substrate's own law and would forbid behaviour Moneta explicitly permits — and which the test suite explicitly pins. SPEC.md board law 3 already says the fix is 'a URI-keyed registry, not a scalar'; the vendor source is the independent second witness for that.
what_MonetaConfig_ephemeral_guarantees.also_true: make_ephemeral defaults use_real_usd=False (mock target), no snapshot/WAL paths -> fully in-memory, needs no OpenUSD. Pinned by tests/test_moneta_runtime.py:42 test_ephemeral_path_is_pxr_free, which asserts in a CLEAN subprocess that 'pxr' not in sys.modules. Any M1 change that pulls pxr into the import path of moneta_runtime turns that test red.

the_two_authorities_to_reconcile_not_tri.defects: no lock (two threads can both see None and both construct), and keyed on NOTHING — a re-pointed project_path silently keeps serving the old store

the_two_authorities_to_reconcile_not_tri.shape: _MONETA_STORE = None; _MONETA_STORE_KEY: Optional[str] = None; _MONETA_LOCK = threading.Lock(). Resolution at :415-437 takes the lock (:424), returns the cached store iff the key matches (:425-426), otherwise CLOSES the previous store to release its URI lock (:429) and rebuilds (:435-436). Teardown at :442-449.

tests_that_hold_two_or_more_live_stores_.method: Mechanical scan (functions with >= 2 store constructions) followed by a HAND READ of every candidate. Only hand-verified cases are listed here; the scan's false positives (nested-def and module-level attribution artifacts in test_sqlite_store.py, test_pipeline_efficiency.py, test_ledger_moneta_seam.py) are excluded, as are sequential open/close pairs (test_moneta_crucible.py:111,:130; test_moneta_integration.py:122; test_moneta_runtime.py:68; test_w3_harden_concurrency.py:193) which do NOT hold two at once.

cases.sites: nested build_state() constructs a fresh ephemeral handle at tests/test_moneta_integration.py:91; the assertion at :99 is `assert build_state() == build_state()`
cases.why_it_breaks_under_a_scalar: Python evaluates the left call fully, then the right — the FIRST handle is never closed before the SECOND is built. Two live ephemeral handles, distinct URIs. A scalar singleton returns the first store to the second call and the determinism assertion becomes vacuous (or the second construction is refused outright).

cases.sites: :107 s1 = MonetaBackedStore.from_storage_dir(tmp_path/'proj'); :110 a SECOND from_storage_dir on the SAME dir inside pytest.raises; :115 a third after s1.close()
cases.why_it_matters: This test PINS the URI-keyed semantics directly: same URI -> refuse while live; after release -> acquire cleanly AND reload prior state. Any M1 design must keep same-URI refusal AND post-close reacquisition. It is the single most load-bearing test for the handle law.

cases.sites: :63 a = from_storage_dir(tmp_path); :67 second from_storage_dir(tmp_path) inside pytest.raises
cases.why_it_matters: Second, independent pin of same-URI refusal, and it asserts on the EXCEPTION IDENTITY ('Locked' in type name, or 'already held' in message). A registry that refuses with a different exception type/message turns this red.

cases.sites: :87 spawns TWO OS child processes each opening the same store dir; :112 the parent then opens it again
cases.why_it_matters: Asserts opened == 2, i.e. the lock is deliberately PROCESS-LOCAL and cross-process opens are NOT excluded. An M1 fix that reaches for a filesystem lock to 'do it properly' turns this red — the test is a receipt of a KNOWN limit, not a bug to fix. Changing it is a finding to report, not a diff to land (AGENTS.md §4).

cases.sites: :51 primary = MemoryStore(tmp_path/'.synapse'); :52 shadow = MonetaBackedStore(make_ephemeral(...)); :53 ShadowMemoryStore(primary, shadow)
cases.why_it_breaks_under_a_scalar: A jsonl store and a Moneta store live SIMULTANEOUSLY, by construction — the whole point of the shadow. Used by every test in the file that calls _shadow(). A single global 'the store' has no way to represent this.

cases.sites: :105 and :106 — a Moneta-backed store and a jsonl store built back to back, then rank(moneta.search(q)) == rank(jsonl.search(q))
cases.why_it_breaks_under_a_scalar: The comparison is meaningless unless both are live at the same instant.

cases.sites: :268 handle = make_ephemeral(dim=DIM); :269 s1 = MonetaBackedStore(handle, ...); :275 s2 = MonetaBackedStore(handle, ...) — a DIFFERENT embedder over the SAME handle
cases.why_it_matters: Two live STORE objects over ONE handle. The docstring states the invariant explicitly: 'the handle owns the ECS, not the store wrapper.' Any registry must key on the HANDLE/URI, not on the store wrapper object, or this becomes a false conflict.

cases.sites: :289 handle; :290 s1 (dim 256); :293 s2 (dim 384) over the same handle
cases.why_it_matters: Same shape as above and it asserts s1.embedder_id != s2.embedder_id, so BOTH wrappers must remain alive and independently interrogable.

sites: tests/test_moneta_store.py:36 (the _store() fixture — every test in the file inherits this)
tests_relying_on_a_unique_auto_generated.the_constraint: Every one of these depends on ephemeral() minting a FRESH uuid4 URI per call. If M1 introduces a registry that normalizes, canonicalizes, interns, or reuses ephemeral URIs, these 18 sites start colliding with each other and the suite goes red in a way that looks like a substrate bug. Key the registry on the storage_uri AS GIVEN; do not rewrite it.

2_constraints_m1_must_not_break.design_note_for_the_forge: The substrate already implements the correct data structure (moneta/api.py:169 `_ACTIVE_URIS: set[str]`). SYNAPSE's two authorities are a keyless unlocked scalar (store.py:1516) and a single-key locked scalar (ledger.py:320-322). SPEC.md board law 3 forbids adding a THIRD. The shape that satisfies every test above is one URI-keyed registry with the lock, replacing both — not a new module alongside them.

red_2_backfill.verdict: GENUINE LOGIC FAILURE. Deterministic, mechanism proven, and bisected to a single commit.
red_2_backfill.introduced_by_subject: feat(memory): W3-STORE cortex_root materialized - typed root, write/query, dual-write armed [receipt: W3-STORE.json]  (2026-08-13)

mechanism_proven_at_master.finding: MonetaBackedStore.from_storage_dir attaches a JSONL DUAL-WRITE SINK - the instance attribute `_jsonl_net` is itself a MemoryStore over the SAME storage_dir. backfill_to_moneta (python/synapse/memory/backfill.py:75-79) opens the target that way and then calls target.add(memory) for each of the 7 memories it just READ out of that same memory.jsonl. Each add() therefore re-writes the record into the source file.
isolation_probe_step_by_step: after a second MemoryStore(storage_dir) ctor + _wait_loaded(): 7 lines  (not the cause)
after MonetaBackedStore.from_storage_dir(): 7 lines  (construction alone is not the cause)
after 7 x target.add(): 14 lines  <-- THE CAUSE
mechanism_proven_at_master.confirmation: getattr(target, '_jsonl_net') is a live <synapse.memory.store.MemoryStore> object. Decrypting both files and comparing as SETS gives only-in-before=0 and only-in-after=0 - every added line is an exact duplicate of an existing one, not new or altered content.

why_it_is_not_environmental: Not key-dependent: the damage is LINE COUNT (7 -> 14) and byte length (4891 -> 9782, exactly 2x), not ciphertext tails. It would fail identically with encryption off.

Not clock-dependent: measured backfill elapsed = 0.195s against MemoryStore._flush_interval = 2.0s (python/synapse/memory/store.py:196), so the 2-second background flusher never fires. _flush_max = 50 (store.py:197) against 7 buffered lines, so the capacity trigger never fires either. Neither background-writer path is involved.
Not locale-dependent: no formatting or collation is in play.
Deterministic: 3 consecutive runs at master, 3 failures. Fails both in isolation and inside the full suite, with the same assertion.
red_2_backfill.correction_to_my_own_earlier_packet: In section 1 I recorded a reading that the differing ciphertext tails looked like a per-write nonce. That reading is REFUTED by this probe - it is duplicate-append, not nonce churn. I flagged it at the time as a hypothesis with no probe behind it; the probe now says otherwise. Routing on the nonce reading would have sent this to the crypto layer instead of the dual-write sink.
red_2_backfill.blast_radius_stated_precisely: The duplicate records land in the SOURCE memory.jsonl - the durable store the backfill promised to leave untouched. On reload MemoryStore keys _memories by id, so a re-open dedupes back to 7, which is why tests/test_backfill.py::test_execute_backfills_and_verifies still passes (source_count == deposited == 7). The observable damage is therefore (a) the file doubling on every backfill run, and (b) a violated 'source untouched (reversible)' guarantee - NOT count corruption or lost content. Do not escalate this as data loss; do not dismiss it as cosmetic.
red_2_backfill.not_fixed: No fix applied. The test is correct as written; the assertion is doing exactly its job.
